The sun was setting and people were sitting outside.

You came back very late last night. Did you find the square?
I did. I was strolling along the harbor when I heard music, so I followed it.
That was the summer festival. I was working here until ten, so I missed the beginning.
Out of nowhere, a crowd appeared around the fountain. Everyone was dancing.
The old women dance there every year. My grandmother was dancing in that square when she was twenty.
At that point, I realized I was the only tourist. Nobody was taking photographs.
That is the real festival. The tourists usually stay on the terraces near the gate, so they never see it.
The atmosphere was completely different at night.
And what were you doing when that happened?

Last Friday I finished work early and I walked down to the river. The sun was setting behind the castle, and the whole street was orange. People were sitting outside on every terrace, and a man was playing the accordion near the bridge. I was looking for a quiet table when I noticed a small door I had never seen before. Inside there was a tiny courtyard with six tables and no menu at all. The owner cooked one dish that night, and it was the best meal I ate all year.

You are standing in the main square. Two hundred years ago this was a fish market, and every morning at five o'clock the boats were arriving from the islands. The fountain in the centre was the only source of fresh water in the town, so people were meeting here long before they were shopping here. Look up at the yellow building on your right. While the workers were repairing the roof in 1998, they found a Roman wall under the floor. Today you can see it through the glass at your feet.

He was strolling along the harbor with no plan, and the sun was setting behind the walls. He was looking for a quiet table when he heard music somewhere behind the terraces. He followed the sound and stumbled upon a small square he had never seen. Out of nowhere a crowd appeared around the fountain, and the old women started dancing. At that point he realized he was the only tourist in the square.
